title: Landslide & debris flow
tldr: Move away from a slide area if you can do so safely, and obey evacuation warnings. Avoid steep slopes, channels and places downhill from recent burns during heavy rain. Do not cross moving debris or enter a fresh slide to inspect it.
steps: New ground cracks, tilting trees, unusual runoff or rumbling warrant immediate caution and a call to local authorities.
Use an official safe route rather than following a drainage channel.
Mud and debris can sweep away vehicles and hide damaged road surfaces.
Give the location and visible hazards to emergency services; keep others out.
next: Return only after local authorities assess stability. Contact a qualified professional about slope or structural damage.
watch: Another slide can follow the first, especially during continued rain.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Stay away from channels, fresh debris and unstable slopes after the first movement. Do not cross the slide to check a house or search for belongings. Choose a destination outside the runout area rather than simply a higher point on the same unstable slope.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
